claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my child Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you. I'll ask a few questions about Alex to help determine your eligibility.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, I need to ask a few more questions.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar) or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any of that. Actually, Alex has started an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's helpful information.

Could you tell me whether Alex's apprenticeship is an **unpaid** apprenticeship, or does Alex receive payment for it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's a paid apprenticeship - Alex gets paid for the work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on the UK government rules, I now have enough information to make an eligibility decision for Alex.

Since Alex is 17 and has started a **paid apprenticeship in England**, the rules state that Child Benefit stops when a child "starts an apprenticeship in England." This is specifically listed as one of the circumstances where Child Benefit eligibility ends.

Let me confirm this and provide you with my final assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm afraid you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Reason:** Alex is 17 years old and has started an apprenticeship in England. Under UK Child Benefit rules, eligibility for Child Benefit stops when a child starts an apprenticeship in England. This applies even though Alex is under 20.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if they leave the apprenticeship and return to approved full-time education or training), you may be able to claim again at that point.

If you have any questions or would like to discuss this further, please feel free to ask.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and has started a paid apprenticeship in England. According to UK Child Benefit eligibility rules, you will stop getting Child Benefit if your child 'starts an apprenticeship in England'. This applies regardless of whether the apprenticeship is paid or unpaid. Therefore, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
